findings.summary: The constant rule needs three or more per-job items; the accepted reading said more than one.
findings.evidence: The reading assumption says 'all identical when there is more than one item'. `per_item_values` returns None when `entries.len() < 3`, and a unit test asserts two equal items are not constant. The planned demonstration the critic accepted already had this, so it is a known deviation, but two equal items are never flagged.

findings.summary: The judge relies on text heuristics and does not convert units, so it rarely sends anything back on the gate's usual wording.
findings.evidence: The phrase is taken from text between 'the' and 'it prints'. The range must be numeric after 'expected range', with no unit conversion. The gate's example wording ('the landing time it prints is within the expected range taken from the commit times in history.json') gives no numeric range, and no line of today's output holds 'landing time', so such runs are only recorded. This fails open and the reading, CHANGELOG and D183 state it, but the failure class gets fewer send-backs than the request might suggest. My run of real `status --snapshot` on the evidence snapshot printed no per-job list (result about the snapshot only).

findings.summary: Two related changes reach every job: a new sentence in every producer brief and redaction of cited criterion commands in every verdict.
findings.evidence: briefs.rs `checks_before_verifier_section` gains a paragraph on all producer briefs. verification.rs now calls `redact_all` on each criterion's `commands`. The redactor is deterministic, so matching only becomes more correct, but each criterion with commands adds a separate gitleaks scan. Batching them into one `redact_all` call would avoid the extra scans.

findings.summary: When the producer is sent back for another reason, it does not see a records run that had no problem.
findings.evidence: `append_records_problems` returns the text unchanged unless a run has a Problem verdict.

findings.summary: Selection matches 'real records' only by lower-casing; the gate also treats hyphens as spaces.
findings.evidence: `select` uses `to_ascii_lowercase` and `contains("real records")`, while `check_records_measure` searches `records_measure_forms`, which reads hyphens and underscores as spaces. A criterion that passes the gate with 'real-records' would run nothing.

summary: Pass. The change makes Athena run each behavior criterion that names real records and gives a `status --snapshot` command. It runs in Athena's own process, after the producer's report and in-loop checks and before the verifier, against the job's evidence snapshot. A constant per-job list or a figure outside the stated range joins the existing single send-back, carrying the command, the judged lines and the output. Every run appears in the verifier's brief as Athena's own run, which the verifier must repeat and cite. A missing or unreadable snapshot ends the job before any verifier runs, naming the snapshot by placeholder. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core records_` (98 passed, including 11 new fake-producer `records_loop_*` tests and 13 unit tests) and `cargo test -p athena-context records_run` (2 passed). I also ran the real `status --snapshot` on the evidence snapshot to see which lines the judge would match. fmt, clippy and the full test suite come from Athena's recorded CI run, which passed. The CHANGELOG entry and decision D183 are additions only, and every changed file is on the deliverables list. Findings are minor: the constant rule needs three or more items where the reading said more than one; the range rule rarely fires on the gate's usual non-numeric wording, a documented limit; and the producer brief sentence and the redaction of cited commands apply to every job.
